title: Traditional Chinese Medicine as Add-on Treatment for Helicobacter Pylori Infection
author: Xiaobei Si
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgnijvce

steps.title: Perform Literature Search
steps.instruction: Conduct a systematic search for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (SR/MAs) comparing Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and Western medicine for Helicobacter pylori infection.

substeps.instruction: Search the following databases up until December 16th, 2018: MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure Database (CNKI), Chinese VIP Information (VIP), Chinese Medical Databases (CMB), and Wan-Fang Database.
Include academic journals, dissertations, and conference proceedings regardless of gray literature status.
Search the reference lists of identified studies for additional relevant titles.

Utilize the Medline search strategy: (#1 “Helicobacter pylori”[Mesh] OR Helicobacter pylori[Title/Abstract]) AND (#2 “Medicine, Chinese Traditional”[Mesh] OR herbal medicine OR herb* OR Chinese medicine OR traditional Chinese Medicine OR Chinese Traditional Medicine OR TCM[Title/Abstract] OR herbal formula decoction OR proprietary medicine OR patent medicine) AND (#3 “meta-analysis”[Publication Type] OR meta analysis[Title/Abstract] OR meta-analysis[Title/Abstract] OR systemic review[Title/Abstract]).

steps.title: Screen Literature
steps.instruction: Screen retrieved trials using a two-step process performed independently by two reviewers.

substeps.instruction: Step 1: Perform potential screening of titles and abstracts for relevant articles.
Step 2: Retrieve and screen full texts based on inclusion and exclusion criteria.
Resolve any disagreements through discussion or by consulting another specialist.

steps.title: Apply Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria
steps.instruction: Evaluate studies based on the following specific criteria to determine eligibility for the overview.

substeps.instruction: Inclusion Criteria: (1) Patients: Hp infectors (with or without related diseases like gastritis/ulcer) diagnosed according to the 'Fifth Chinese National Consensus Report on the management of Helicobacter pylori infection'; (2) Interventions: TCM (herbs, proprietary medicine, or extractives) combined with PTT (PPI plus two antibiotics) or BCQT (PPI, bismuth, and two antibiotics); (3) Control: PTT or BCQT only; (4) Outcomes: Main outcome is eradication rate; secondary outcomes include side effect rate, remission rate of digestive symptoms, and ulcer healing rate/total effectiveness rate; (5) Study type: Systematic review and/or meta-analyses (SR/MA).

Exclusion Criteria: (1) Redundant publications; (2) Studies titled 'meta-analysis' or 'systemic review' that do not perform meta-synthesis calculations; (3) Systemic reviews of in vitro studies; (4) Articles published as abstracts or protocols.

steps.title: Extract Data
steps.instruction: Two reviewers independently extract data from the included SR/MAs using piloted forms.

substeps.instruction: Extract items including: authors, publication year, sample size, intervention groups, main outcome (eradication rate), and secondary outcomes (remission of digestive symptoms, healing of digestive ulcers, and side effects).

steps.title: Assess Methodological Quality
steps.instruction: Two reviewers independently assess the quality of each included review using the AMSTAR scale.

substeps.instruction: Use a piloted form to evaluate 11 AMSTAR items (e.g., a priori design, duplicate selection/extraction, comprehensive search, grey literature status, list of studies, characteristics of studies, scientific quality assessment, appropriate use of quality in conclusions, combination methods, publication bias, and conflict of interest).
Score each item: 1 point for 'yes' (explicitly met) and 0 points for 'no', 'cannot answer', or 'not applicable'.
Calculate the total score for each SR/MA.

steps.title: Assess Reporting Characteristics
steps.instruction: Two reviewers (Xiao-Bei Si and Shuai Wang) independently assess the level of evidence and summarize each outcome using the GRADE approach.
